barCharacter: Vera Oberlin. She is the cast member who sits at the top of the hierarchy and judges everyone else; her comedy is the status she takes for granted ('cover up the literal murder I've committed... Right?', 'Right. Now.'). That is Vesper's job as a star with standards. Valerie (bored deadpan shopkeeper) is the runner-up on register, but she has fewer lines and less of a judging role. The corpus has 9 Vera lines, so her 12 are those 9 plus the 3 narrator lines that write her (#53, #54, #55).

headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar. Cover the names and Vera's lines are about Vera: her career, her beauty, her murder, her advisor. Each one carries a status assumption only she would make. Vesper's best twelve do hold up (the sixty-two retirement, forty years of screening, 'Mostly mine'), and those are hers because they lean on her age and her shift. Across the rest of the bank the identification comes from the word 'caller' (in 51 of 191 lines, and 19 lines open with it) and the radio nouns, not from sentence shape. Strip 'caller' and swap fader for minibar and most react and cardReact lines become Maximilian's: same flat 'Short. Shorter.' rhythm, same 'Say it again, slower' approval. The other two stars' banks contain near-verbatim twins: 'Frost. I am opening the door. And not for cheese.' (Maximilian and Pixel), 'She is right. I hate that she is right.' (Maximilian), 'You did exactly what I said? Nobody does that.' and 'Brock. You did good. You did so good.' (Pixel), plus 'That is all? I have had longer receipts.' against 'That's it? Caller, I've had longer sneezes.' A voice that its rivals can say word for word is not unmistakable.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Tie. Vesper is economical. Most lines are under ten words and turn on the last two or three ('Mostly mine.', 'Nobody came.', 'That was weather.'), which is what the bar does too. Vera's twelve include flat plot hooks (#46, #50) that are no better built than ours. Where Vesper loses ground is the middle of the bank. Cuts and picks restate the suitor's gimmick before turning it ('Dash, you tested two versions of yourself tonight. Neither one converted.'), and a few lines explain the joke after landing it ('That's my whole type, apparently.', 'Highest compliment I've got.'). That pulls her down to level, not below.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar. 'My career on not dating losers like you', 'cover up the literal murder', 'tame her hair with a cattle prod' and 'Right. Now.' get clipped because the status move is outrageous. Vesper has two clip-worthy lines (Moon and June retiring in sixty-two, 'Not four. I've cut people for four.') and a handful of good ones. Her charm is mood, and mood does not clip. Nothing in the bank is as big as the bar's worst crime.

templates: Gimmick reversal: say the suitor's own jargon back to them as the cut or verdict (closing your ticket, marking you as spam, moving you to junk, ending the trial, muting you, you've arrived / this is your exit, opening the door not for the cheese, past your date, nobody recommended you). Roughly 20 lines, including nearly every cut. Maximilian and Pixel run the same template on the same nouns, so the joke belongs to the suitor's bible and not to Vesper.

Approval + 'Don't [your gimmick]': 'That one converted, salesman. Don't put it on a slide.', 'Don't send the survey', 'Don't ruin it', 'Don't get used to it', 'Don't screenshot it', 'Don't apologise', 'Don't faint, and don't send an invoice', 'Don't recalculate'. 13 lines contain Don't. It is the default charmed/pick shape.

'Say it again, slower': 'Say thee again, Quill. Slower.', 'That was terrible. Say it again, slower.', 'Say the price again. Slowly.', 'Read me the trophy shelf again.', 'Say that word again.', 'Call me that again. Quietly.' Six lines, mostly cardReact 'on', and the same approval each time.

One-on-one 'strip the gimmick, ask for the secret': 'No variants...', 'Nobody's on hold, Tilly...', 'Prince, no fee. No urgency...', 'Nav, no destination tonight...', 'Nobody's watching, Vex...', 'Just you and me, Quill...', 'Turn the dashboard off, Dash...'. All 16 one-on-one lines are the CAST.md Secret column turned into a question. Vesper has no way to know those secrets, so she reads like the writer's room.

'Caller, [generic rebuke].': 19 lines open on 'Caller,' and the rest of the sentence is a line any star could say ('Caller, I didn't open you for a lecture.', 'Caller, I did not ask to be spotted.', 'Caller, this isn't the greeting card aisle.'). The tag is doing the voice work.

'It's late' as the reason: 'It's two in the morning, Brock.', 'Smaller words, caller. It's two in the morning.', 'Stop reading me decimals. It's late.', 'after midnight' twice, 'after three'. Seven lines give the same alibi.

(Vex's secret). This is not a listed rule, but it breaks the show's logic.
biggestGap: Almost every react, cut, pick and one-on-one gets its laugh from the suitor's own gimmick said back to them (ticket, spam, fee, recalculate, cheese, unfinished poem), which is why Maximilian and Pixel land the same jokes nearly word for word; Vera's laughs come from what Vera takes for granted about herself. In the next pass, give Vesper her own X-but-secretly-Y (the untouchable host who keeps the line open at 3 a.m. because nobody else calls, and who has outlived every caller and format) and rewrite those categories so the suitor's gimmick is only the setup while the turn lands on her (her forty years, her dead air, her callers who never called back, the trucker), then delete any line that still works with Maximilian's name on it.

notes: Bar file present and read in full (88 entries plus narration); charm-notes.md read too. The bank holds 191 lines; 112 are listed as generic, stock, self-explaining or templated (some fit more than one bucket, and each is counted once under the first that fits). The strongest material clusters where the format forces Vesper to talk about herself: twistIntro (nearly all twelve are hers), intro, outro, hold, reveal ('nobody came' / 'Nobody tuned in') and the ex lines. The weakest is where she reacts to a suitor, because those slots were written from the suitors' CAST rows. The porch-light reveal and 'Go to sleep. I won't.' already hint at the loneliness that could be her Y; that thread is the thing to pull. Also worth protecting: 'That wasn't an answer. That was weather.', 'I think I got this letter in nineteen ninety-eight.', 'I like expensive things and long silences. How do you afford either?', 'Read me the worst thing in your logs. I've heard worse. Mostly mine.' 'Mm' opens four lines and 'caller' appears in 27% of the bank; both are tags, not voice. The dedication move (four 'song called X' lines) is the most Vesper-specific device in the persona, yet it appears only in four cringing reacts. It could carry cuts instead of the gimmick reversals. The ex line 'Draw your own conclusions, callers.' explains a joke the previous sentence already landed. Cross-star duplicates were checked against maximilian.json and pixel.json in the same folder.
